subject: Recap + network asks for Private VPC evaluation (BlueGrid)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Keller <sofie.keller@bluegrid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + network asks for Private VPC evaluation (BlueGrid)

Hi Sofie / Tom —

Thanks again for a constructive call today. Quick recap and the minimal networking info we'll need to evaluate a Private VPC/on-prem deployment for BlueGrid so engineering can size the config and surface any blockers before we proceed with a pilot.

Summary from our side
- Deployment modes discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC (your preference for regulated workloads). You confirmed priority is data isolation + egress control.
- Primary constraints you mentioned: overlap with existing on-prem CIDRs, requirement for outbound allowlisting, and internal security review window in mid-September.

Network items we need to qualify feasibility (please see attached checklist):
1) Preferred connectivity pattern: PrivateLink endpoint into your VPC, direct VPC peering, or VPN/transit gateway? If you have a strong preference call that out.
2) CIDR ranges for the BlueGrid VPCs we would peer/connect to (including any on-prem overlapping ranges).
3) Egress/ingress firewall requirements: list of required destination ports and whether any deep packet inspection TLS proxies are in path.
4) A BLUF on whether you require inbound connections to Redwood-managed subnets (usually not; we initiate outbound connections into your VPC via PrivateLink) — helps determine NAT/route setup.
5) IP allowlist: do you need a fixed set of Redwood egress IPs or will PrivateLink/Interface endpoints suffice? If allowlist required, we will provide a short list of candidate IPs once we choose connection type.

Next steps / proposed timeline
- You: share topology doc or network diagram (simple PNG/PDF).
- We: produce a short connection proposal (1–2 pages) and a tentative IP list for allowlist and sample route table changes by Friday (8/7).
- Joint: schedule a 30m network ops sync (we can include Marissa and Ben from our side).

Attachments: redwood-vpc-preflight-checklist.pdf (see highlighted required fields).

If you want, Ben can jump into your network ops call to walk through PrivateLink vs peering tradeoffs.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood-vpc-preflight-checklist.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Sofie Keller <sofie.keller@bluegrid.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@bluegrid.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + network asks for Private VPC evaluation (BlueGrid)

Thanks Alex — good summary. A couple of clarifications from our end: 

- Connectivity preference: our security team prefers PrivateLink (interface endpoints) where possible because it avoids route table changes and limits attack surface. However, if we hit throughput or cost limits, we may fall back to VPC peering.
- CIDRs: primary VPC is 10.40.0.0/16 (us-east-1). We also have an on-prem range 172.16.10.0/24 that is currently NAT'd behind our transit gateway — let us know if that causes issues.
- Allowlist policy: we will not accept large dynamic IP ranges. We need a primary list of 3–5 egress IPs to put in our perimeter ACLs.
- TLS inspection: we do have a TLS proxy for some outbound flows; we will confirm whether it will break mTLS or token-based auth.

Action items on our side:
- I'll upload a simple topology PNG to the shared drive by EOD (Tom will attach).
- Security will review PrivateLink tradeoffs and should be able to give an answer by 8/20.

Happy to schedule the netops sync — can we do Friday 8/8 at 11:00am ET?

—Sofie
Sofie Keller
Head of Cloud Ops, BlueGrid Analytics
sofie.keller@bluegrid.ai | +1 (617) 444-9001

Attachment: BG-topology-draft.png (PNG, 85KB)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Keller <sofie.keller@bluegrid.ai>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@bluegrid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + network asks for Private VPC evaluation (BlueGrid)

Thanks Sofie — that helps a lot. Friday 8/8 11:00am ET works for our team; I’ll send a calendar invite.

Ben / Marissa — looping you in for the technical sync. Based on BlueGrid notes:
- Primary ask: PrivateLink preferred, but they need a small fixed allowlist if PrivateLink is unsuitable.
- BlueGrid VPC: 10.40.0.0/16; on-prem: 172.16.10.0/24 behind TGW (possible asymmetric routing).

Proposed immediate items from our side (we’ll deliver by EOD):
1) Short two-page connection proposal with PrivateLink and peering pros/cons specific to BlueGrid.
2) Candidate static egress IP list (3 addresses) if they need allowlist entries. Note: static egress IPs will be advertised from our egress NAT layer; availability depends on customer region/config.
3) A checklist for TLS proxy compatibility (questions for their security team).

Marissa: can you prepare the candidate IPs and a short note on whether asymmetric routing with their TGW is a blocker? Also include any tenancy/placement concerns for us-east-1.

I’ve attached the preflight checklist and an example topology (from a recent deployment) for reference.

Thanks —
Alex

Attachments: redwood-vpc-preflight-checklist.pdf, example-topology.png
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Recap + network asks for Private VPC evaluation (BlueGrid)

(Internal notes for track / handoff to engineering)

Quick technical summary for the internal ticket we should open:
- BlueGrid prefers PrivateLink. Good because it avoids route table changes. We'll need them to provision interface endpoints in their subnets and share the subnet IDs and AZ mapping.
- CIDR overlap: no overlap between 10.40.0.0/16 and our typical infra ranges, but their on-prem 172.16.10.0/24 is OK as long as the TGW NAT is consistent.
- Candidate static egress IPs (initial): 54.183.12.45, 54.183.12.46, 54.183.12.47 — mark as tentative until legal confirms egress policy.
- TLS proxy: if their TLS inspection terminates client-side TLS, token-based auth should still work but mTLS breakage is possible — we need their security team to confirm whether interception is TLS-terminating or passthrough.
- Ops asks for:
  * Subnet IDs where they can host interface endpoints (private subnets preferred).
  * Confirmation of whether PrivateLink traffic may traverse their transit gateway.
  * Any port restrictions on port 443 outbound.

Action items assigned:
- Marissa: validate ip ownership and egress advert method (EOD 8/7).
- Ben: prepare a short runbook for interface endpoint setup and required IAM permissions.
- Alex: confirm meeting time and send invite to BlueGrid.

I’ll open INFRA-9649 and drop these notes in the ticket.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
